 Parks & Recreation Commission, May 9, 2024  Page 2 of 2
   MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  April 11, 2024

Chairperson Ally Hernandez called the meeting to order at 6:07 p.m.
Commission members present were Anthony Armendarez, Francisco Berberabe, David
King, Don Valenzuela, and Briana Martinez. Commissioner Monique Napier, Victor
Juan, Steve Garcia, and Maria Carbajal was absent.
Staff present included Director of Recreation and Park Services Allan Perdomo,
Recreation Superintendent Sonia Batres, Recreation Supervisor Maurisabel Camacho,
Recreation Supervisor Pati Garcia, Recreation Coordinator Allison Franco, Recreation
Leader III Juanita Porras, and Office Assistant III Lorraine Mendoza.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Berberabe motioned to accept the March 14, 2024 meeting minutes with
an amendment made. Commissioner Martinez seconded the motion. All in favor.
REPORTS

Presentation: Recap EGG-Stravagant 2024

Superintendent Batres gave a recap on the 2024 EGG-Stravagant Event. Due to
inclement weather, the event was relocated from the City Hall Lawn to the Norwalk Arts
& Sports Complex. The day included egg hunts, bunny photos, arts and crafts, and a
Health and Wellness Expo. Over 25,000 pieces of candy and Easter eggs were
distributed. The egg hunts were expanded and times were revised to make everything
run smoothly. Approximately two egg hunts were held per hour. There were special
prizes; 375 photos were sold; and when the crafts ran out, Public Safety came in
distributing color books. The City collaborated with the California State University of
Long Beach to hold the Health and Wellness Expo. A shuttle service helped shuttle
participants in from City Hall. This form of transportation will continue being offered
moving forward. The event was a success with positive feedback.

Presentation: Artastic Recap 2024

Recreation Supervisor Garcia presented on The Artastic Event held on March 15. The
event consisted of a Community Student Art Competition; entertainment; live
demonstrations; a Scholastic Book Fair ; an Art Box Exhibit; a Chalk Art Competition;
Arts and Craft area; dancing in the streets; Art Walk vendors ; and food trucks. The
Community Student Art Competition consisted of three high schools and four middle
schools. The entertainment was provided by Creative Little Hands; Miniachis De
Norwalk; And Dance; Empowered Movement Dance Company; and Kids Talent
Academy. The live demonstrations included 3-D chalk art and a paint demo. The
Scholastic Book Fair joined the event for its eighth year. The Cultural Arts Center Art

Box Exhibit had 30 participants. This ran for three weeks and artists had the opportunity
to sell their artwork. The Chalk Art Competition had 15 participants. Supervisor Garcia
thanked the Commissioners for judging the event where prizes were awarded in three
categories. The Transportation department shuttled approximately 80 people from City
Hall to the Artastic event. The event was a great success.

Presentation: Overview of Cultural Arts Programs

Recreation Leader III Porras reported on the Cultural Arts Center programs and
activities. She shared details on the classes, programs, workshops, museums, gallery,
and special events. The age groups for art classes and Creative Li’L Hands were
shared, as well as the days and times. Programs include Miniachis De Norwalk, Kids
Adventure Camp, Family Beach Bus Trip, and a variety of workshops. She also shared
all of the Museum operating hours. The submittal process was provided on how to
submit artwork at the Mary Paxon Gallery. The exhibit normally runs for three weeks
and all proceeds go directly to the artist.The upcoming special events include Tea Time
at the Hargitt House; an Ice Cream Social; Dinner and a Movie; along with other free
events.

Presentation: Park Projects Update

Director Allan Perdomo updated the Commissioners on the ongoing park projects. He
spoke briefly on the upcoming ribbon cutting events for Vista Verde Park, Holifield Park,
and Bob White Dog. At all the ribbon cutting events there will be a ceremony, prizes and
giveaways. Director Perdomo listed a variety of Earth Day activities to celebrate the
day. The Sproul Museum roofing project is completed. The snack bar renovations at
Holifield Park is completed and the Lakeside Park snack bar is currently being
renovated. The lighting at all baseball and softball fields will be improved. Norwalk Park
playground will be the biggest renovation project. Hermosillo Park is currently working
with contractors. Once it’s been finalized, a presentation will be provided to the
Commissioners.

STAFF COMMENTS

Director Perdomo shared a list of upcoming Recreation events. The Mayor’s Prayer
Breakfast still has tickets available for purchase. The Norwalk 5K registration is going
strong. Many sponsorships have come in. Director Perdomo requested that the
Commissioners come out to the 5K event to participate, support, and volunteer. There
will be a Scholas event at the Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex on May 4 and May
5.On May 8 and May 9, the Recreation Department will hold an in-service training for all

department staff. There will be a Meet and Greet Dinner to get to know fellow
commissioners. The dinner will be on Friday, May 31, in the Sproul Reception Center.

COMMISISONER’S COMMENTS

Vice Chair King – Thanked everyone and thought the Artastic Event was great.
Commissioner Armendarez – Congratulated Chairperson Ally Hernandez on receiving
Woman of the Year. Attended and loved the Easter event. Appreciated how welcoming
everyone has been.
Commissioner Martinez - Shared that she has been a Commissioner for years and
this has been the best year so far. Is very excited with all the information and events.
Commissioner Berberabe – Also feels he has received the most information and
learned a lot from this Commission compared to past years. Thanked the Director and
the staff.
Commissioner Valenzuela – Complimented the staff on all the positive attitudes. Had
a concern with the stop sign at Sproul Street and Clarkdale Avenue.
Chair Hernandez – Stated that she enjoys working along side all the Commissioners
and staff. Agreed with fellow Commissioners that the staff is doing a great job. Very
excited about all the upcoming programs and events.
NEXT MEETING
May 9, 2024
There being no further business to discuss, Chairperson Hernandez motioned to
adjourn the meeting. Seconded by Vice Chair King. All in favor. The meeting adjourned
at 7:12 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________
Chairperson Ally Hernandez
